PRE_STATED_STRUCTURAL_SUSPICIONS.S1_freewheel_deleted: Read from RF_C9_L10_t35.cir line 154 BEFORE running: 'VGFW3 gfw3 0 PWL(0 0 4400p 0)'. The freewheel nMOS gate is held at 0 V for the entire run, i.e. the freewheel device is PERMANENTLY OFF. The prior agent calls this a 'diode freewheel' relying on the drain-bulk junction. PREDICTION: a buck's charge GAIN (Qdel/Qsup = Vin/Vout > 1) comes ENTIRELY from the freewheel phase, in which the inductor sources charge from GROUND, not from the supply. With no freewheel path, Qdel/Qsup is bounded ABOVE by 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION, minus switch-node and leakage cost. So the prior agent's B3 failure (0.516) and its explanation ('a scale limit, gate charge is the same order as delivered charge') are CONFOUNDED: they never ran a converter that could exceed 1.
PRE_STATED_STRUCTURAL_SUSPICIONS.S1_falsifier: If I measure the freewheel-node current in C9 and find substantial current flowing from ground into na3 during the HS-off phase, S1 is refuted and C9 really does freewheel.
PRE_STATED_STRUCTURAL_SUSPICIONS.S2_junction_is_absent: sg13lv_compat.sp DECLARES ad/as/pd/ps as subckt params but the M1 instance line passes ONLY W and L: 'M1 d g s b sg13g2_nmos W={w} L={l}'. The junction areas are therefore never handed to the model at all. PREDICTION: the drain-bulk diode of XTUFW is effectively absent, so 'diode freewheel' is a mechanism that does not exist in this deck. Falsifier: measurable forward junction current at the FW device during HS-off.
PRE_STATED_STRUCTURAL_SUSPICIONS.S3_C9_is_a_five_variable_change: C9 changes at least five things at once vs C1: freewheel device disabled, LTU 1n->10n, t_on 12->35 ps, fire time 8 ps earlier, OUT switch window retimed. The prior agent's own stated discipline is 'one change at a time so the effect of each is attributable', and their headline +199.65 mV is attributed to ONE of the five ('deleting the freewheel gate transitions is the mechanism'). That attribution is not established by the experiment they ran.
PRE_STATED_STRUCTURAL_SUSPICIONS.S4_the_missing_experiment: C2 and C3 fix only the GATE dead times. Read from RF_C2.cir/RF_C3.cir BEFORE running: in BOTH, the HS pMOS turns ON at 313.137-317.137 ps while the OUT isolation switch does not close until 345.137 ps. So ~28 ps of the 40 ps on-time is spent with the inductor's far end DISCONNECTED. The brief explicitly asked for the OUT timing to be checked; C2/C3 do not change it. A PROPERLY timed synchronous buck -- correct dead time BOTH edges, OUT closed across conduction AND freewheel, and L large enough to be inductive -- was NEVER RUN. I will run it (call it K1). This is the decisive missing experiment and the main thing I am here to supply.
PRE_STATED_STRUCTURAL_SUSPICIONS.S5_C5_was_run_at_the_wrong_L: The prior agent's own finding is that at Ltu = 1 nH, L/R = 2 ps << t_on, so the cell is a RESISTIVE transfer, not an inductive buck, and genuinely inductive operation needs L >> R*t_on ~ 6 nH. But their C5 'textbook order' negative result (-212 mV) was run at L = 1 nH. A textbook buck cannot work at an L where the circuit is not inductive. C5 therefore does not license the conclusion that textbook ordering fails.
PRE_STATED_STRUCTURAL_SUSPICIONS.S6_ideal_bound_depends_on_topology: Qdel/Qsup = Vin/Vout = 1.5666 is the ideal bound for a buck WITH a freewheel. For a series-L resonant transfer with NO freewheel (which is what C9 actually is), the ideal bound is Qdel/Qsup = 1.0 exactly, because every coulomb reaching the bank passed through the supply. Judging C9's 0.516 against 1.5666 is judging it against the wrong bound.
